source.text: Λέγει μοι· Ἁπλότητα ἔχε καὶ ἄκακος γίνου καὶ ἔσῃ ὡς τὰ νήπια τὰ μὴ γινώσκοντα τὴν πονηρίαν τὴν ἀπολλύουσαν τὴν ζωὴν τῶν ἀνθρώπων. 2. πρῶτον μὲν μηδενὸς καταλάλει, μηδὲ ἡδέως ἄκουε καταλαλοῦντος· εἰ δὲ μή, καὶ σὺ ὁ ἀκούων ἔνοχος ἔσῃ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ καταλαλοῦντος, ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς τῇ καταλαλίᾳ ᾗ ἂν ἀκούσῃς· πιστεύσας γὰρ καὶ σὺ αὐτὸς ἕξεις κατὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου. οὕτως οὖν ἔνοχος ἔσῃ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ καταλαλοῦντος. 3. πονηρὰ ἡ καταλαλία, ἀκατάστατον δαιμόνιόν ἐστιν, μηδέποτε εἰρηνεῦον, ἀλλὰ πάντοτε ἐν διχοστασίαις κατοικοῦν. ἀπέχου οὖν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εὐθηνίαν πάντοτε ἕξεις μετὰ πάντων. 4. ἔνδυσαι δὲ τὴν σεμνότητα, ἐν ᾗ οὐδὲν πρόσκομμά ἐστιν πονηρόν, ἀλλὰ πάντα ὁμαλὰ καὶ ἱλαρά. ἐργάζου τὸ ἀγαθόν, καὶ ἐκ τῶν κόπων σου, ὧν ὁ Θεὸς δίδωσίν σοι, πᾶσιν ὑστερουμένοις δίδου ἁπλῶς, μὴ διστάζων τίνι δῷς ἢ τίνι μὴ δῷς. πᾶσιν δίδου· πᾶσιν γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς δίδοσθαι θέλει ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων δωρημάτων. 5. οἱ οὖν λαμβάνοντες ἀποδώσουσιν λόγον τῷ Θεῷ, διατί ἔλαβον καὶ εἰς τί· οἱ μὲν γὰρ λαμβάνοντες θλιβόμενοι οὐ δικασθήσονται, οἱ δὲ ἐν ὑποκρίσει λαμβάνοντες τίσουσιν δίκην. 6. ὁ οὖν διδοὺς ἀθῷός ἐστιν· ὡς γὰρ ἔλαβεν παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου τὴν διακονίαν τελέσαι, ἁπλῶς αὐτὴν ἐτέλεσεν, μηθὲν διακρίνων τίνι δῷ ἢ μὴ δῷ. ἐγένετο οὖν ἡ διακονία αὕτη ἁπλῶς τελεσθεῖσα ἔνδοξος παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ. ὁ οὖν οὕτως ἁπλῶς διακονῶν τῷ Θεῷ ζήσεται. 7. φύλασσε οὖν τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην, ὥς σοι λελάληκα, ἵνα ἡ μετάνοιά σου καὶ τοῦ οἴκου σου ἐν ἁπλότητι εὑρεθῇ, καὶ ἡ καρδία [σου] καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος.

translation.text:
He says to me: Have simplicity[1], and become guileless, and you will be like the little ones who do not know the wickedness that destroys the life of human beings.

First of all, slander no one, and do not listen with pleasure to someone who slanders; otherwise you too, the hearer, will be guilty of the slanderer’s sin if you believe the slander you hear. For by believing it, you yourself also will have something against your brother. Thus you will be guilty of the slanderer’s sin.

Slander is evil; it is a restless demon, never at peace, but always dwelling amid divisions. So keep away from it, and you will always have well‑being with all.

But clothe yourself with dignity, in which there is no evil stumbling block, but all things are smooth and cheerful. Do what is good, and from your labors, which God gives you, give simply to all who are in need, not hesitating as to whom you should give or to whom you should not give. Give to all, for God wants all to be given from his own gifts.

Therefore those who receive will render an account to God why they received and for what; for those who receive while afflicted will not be judged, but those who receive in hypocrisy will pay the penalty.

Therefore the one who gives is innocent[2]; for just as he received from the Lord the ministry to carry out, he carried it out simply, making no distinction as to whom he should give or not give. Thus this ministry, having been carried out simply, became glorious before God. Therefore the one who thus ministers simply to God will live.

So keep this commandment, as I have spoken to you, so that your repentance[b] and that of your household may be found in simplicity[a][7][6][5][4][3], and your heart clean and unstained.

footnotes.text: “Well‑being” renders εὐθηνία, which can also mean “prosperity.” The context (“with all”) suggests good standing and flourishing in relationships rather than material plenty.
“Demon” translates δαιμόνιον; some would paraphrase “evil spirit,” but Hermas’s personification is intentional.
“Dignity” renders σεμνότης; alternatives include “gravity” or “reverent seriousness.”
“Give simply” (ἁπλῶς) can also mean “give generously,” but Hermas emphasizes single‑heartedness as well as liberality.
“Slander” translates καταλαλέω/καταλαλία; “backbiting” is another English option.
“Have something against your brother” reflects a Greek idiom for holding a grievance.
“Ministry” renders διακονία; “service” is possible but less clearly ecclesial.
Or 'Thus this ministry, carried out in simplicity, became glorious with God.'.

Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Hermas uses ἁπλότης as a moral quality of single-heartedness; retaining “simplicity/simply” preserves the thematic thread and avoids narrowing it to mere generosity.
Guileless captures absence of craftiness without implying naïveté; pairs well with ἁπλότης.
“Little ones” conveys tender age and moral exemplar imagery without technicality.
Wickedness signals the moral quality that destroys life in this context.
In moral paraenesis, καταλαλέω commonly denotes slanderous speech against someone; “slander” is clear and specific.
Conveys the culpable attitude in listening to slander.
Legal-moral liability is intended.

theological_decisions.issue: Personified evil in speech ethics (δαιμόνιον for slander)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render δαιμόνιον as “demon,” preserving Hermas’s demonological framing.
alternative_readings: Euphemize as “evil spirit” or metaphorical “evil power”
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas explicitly characterizes slander as a restless δαιμόνιον; retaining “demon” fits early Christian worldview and the text’s personification.

theological_decisions.issue: Scope of almsgiving (“Give to all”) and moral responsibility
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Imperative “Give to all” kept unsoftened; the recipient’s accountability to God balances the exhortation.
alternative_readings: Qualify with prudential limits in the translation

review_passes.summary: The draft is excellent and captures Hermas's moral register well. However, it drops several small but important conjunctions and adverbs (καὶ, πάντοτε, οὖν) that guide the logical flow and emphasis of the exhortation. Restoring these tightens the author's argument.
issues_found: Verse 2: Missed the ascensive καὶ in καὶ σὺ ὁ ἀκούων ('you too, the hearer').
Verse 3: Omitted πάντοτε ('always') in the promise of well-being (καὶ εὐθηνίαν πάντοτε ἕξεις).
Verse 5: Omitted the inferential οὖν ('Therefore') at the start of the sentence (οἱ οὖν λαμβάνοντες).
Verse 6: Translated ἢ as 'and' instead of 'or' in τίνι δῷ ἢ μὴ δῷ.
Verse 6: Omitted the inferential οὖν ('Therefore') in the final sentence (ὁ οὖν οὕτως ἁπλῶς διακονῶν).
Verse 6: Translated the adverb ἁπλῶς as a prepositional phrase 'in simplicity' in the final sentence, breaking the lexical chain of 'simply' established earlier in the verse.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: So the person who gives is innocent. The Lord entrusted him with the work of giving, and he carried it out sincerely, without deciding who should or should not receive help. This sincere service became glorious in God’s sight. Therefore, anyone who serves God in this sincere way will live.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft appropriately clarifies that the ministry is the work of giving and clearly preserves the instruction not to distinguish among recipients. However, replacing the repeated “simply” with “sincerely” shifts the emphasis from uncalculating, nondiscriminatory giving to an inward quality of motive. Revise the repeated rendering so that the conclusion continues to refer to the manner defined by the recipient clause.

base_translation.text: So keep this commandment, as I have spoken to you, so that your repentance and that of your household may be found in simplicity, and your heart clean and unstained.

translation.text: So obey this command, as I have told you, so that you and your household may be found to have repented[a] with sincere and undivided hearts, and so that your own heart may be clean and unstained.

footnotes.text: Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: So obey this command as I have told you. Then you and your household will be found to have repented sincerely, and your heart will be clean and unstained.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: “Obey this command” is a clear, warranted simplification of “keep this commandment.” Revision is needed because “will be found” strengthens the stated purpose into a guarantee, and “sincerely” alone does not adequately carry the simplicity/undividedness of the repentance described. The recommended wording preserves the purpose force while making the ethical sense understandable to modern readers.
